clue.text: Cop must, in crash with cab or US sports car, say

indicators.note: things in a crash are smashed together and come out jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A police officer has to attend a collision between a taxi and an American sports car.
explanation.walkthrough: The car in the surface is part of the definition; 'say' marks a sports car as one example of the class.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage a subcompact is a small car class, which a small sports car can exemplify.

clue.text: Chat maybe opens up in Shakespeare

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the word is written from bottom to top

parts.note: Shakespeare's 'dup' means to open, as in 'dupp'd the chamber door'

explanation.surface: Someone notices that conversation starts up in a Shakespeare play.
explanation.walkthrough: Chat looks like talk but here is a small potato, and a spud is any potato; 'maybe' marks the example.
explanation.definitionFit: A chat is a small potato, so it is one example of a spud, slang for a potato.

clue.text: Source of flummery fit to appear in fog?

indicators.note: one thing appearing in another sits inside it, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: a blur, a haze that hides things
an ague is a fit of fever and shivering

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether nonsense is fit to come out of a fog of confusion.
explanation.walkthrough: Fit reads as suitable, but it is a noun: a bout of fever. A blagueur deals in blague, French for humbug or empty talk.
explanation.definitionFit: A blagueur is a boaster or humbug, someone who produces flummery, meaning empty nonsense and flattery.

clue.text: Plain Scotch (watery?), recipe shown in several bottles

indicators.note: a thing shown in something else is displayed within it, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: wine and spirits are sold by the case of several bottles
R is the abbreviation for recipe, as on prescriptions

explanation.surface: A recipe for watered-down plain Scotch whisky appears in a few bottles.
explanation.walkthrough: Scotch whisky is the picture, but 'Scotch' means Scottish: a carse is a Scottish plain. CA + R + SE.
explanation.definitionFit: Carse is the Scottish word for low fertile land beside a river, so a plain that is often wet.

clue.text: What's associated with chips, containing nothing sour

indicators.note: something containing another holds it inside, so the second piece goes within the first

parts.note: a morse is a walrus, and in Lewis Carroll the Walrus goes with the Carpenter; Chips is a nickname for a carpenter
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: A puzzle asks what goes with chips that has nothing sour in it.
explanation.walkthrough: Chips suggests fried potatoes, but it is the old nickname for a ship's carpenter, partner of the Walrus in Lewis Carroll's 'The Walrus and the Carpenter'.
explanation.definitionFit: Morose and sour are both synonyms for sullen or bad-tempered in mood.

clue.text: Youngster, type that's dropped in

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a young tree or shoot, a sapling
second meaning: a spy or agent placed secretly inside an organization

explanation.surface: A young person is described as the kind who drops in unannounced.
explanation.walkthrough: Youngster reads as a child, but Chambers gives the word for a young tree or sapling.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a sapling and an infiltrator secretly placed among others.

clue.text: Toadie shifting to accept right — tending that way? (7, two words)

indicators.note: shifting letters move them about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A flatterer changes stance to accept the right wing, leaning that way politically.
explanation.walkthrough: R joins the letters of Toadie before they are rearranged. The definition looks back at 'right': the French phrase means to the right.
explanation.definitionFit: French for to the right, describing a direction or leaning towards the right-hand side.

clue.text: Old rose, something from Canterbury see in Church?

indicators.note: one thing in another sits within it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
Canterbury lamb is New Zealand meat from the Canterbury region; 'see' invites a look and dresses it as the archbishop's see

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether something from the see of Canterbury belongs inside a church.
explanation.walkthrough: The see suggests the archbishop, but Canterbury here is the New Zealand province famous for lamb. Rose is the past tense of rise, and clambe an old past tense of climb.
explanation.definitionFit: Clambe is an obsolete past tense of climb, so it once meant went up, the sense of rose.

clue.text: A neat butler organized topping structure

indicators.note: organizing things puts them into a new arrangement, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tidy butler arranged the top layer of something, perhaps a table setting.
explanation.definitionFit: In classical architecture the entablature is the structure resting on top of the columns.

clue.text: Part of cereal diet — see Mali for cooking

indicators.note: ingredients for cooking get mixed and transformed, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A food note says the staple grain of the diet can be found in Mali for cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: Mealies is the South African word for maize, a cereal crop eaten as a staple food.

clue.text: S. Indian tree, once wan, before being brought in

indicators.note: something brought in is taken inside, so this piece goes within the other

parts.note: paly is an old word for pale
a is the abbreviation for ante, Latin for before

explanation.surface: A tree in southern India was once pale before being brought indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once' marks an archaic word, and 'before' gives a letter through the Latin ante.
explanation.definitionFit: The palay is a South Indian tree, a crossword-dictionary name for a native species.

clue.text: High Court order, one on page received by gardener (11, two words)

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, meaning one

indicators.note: what is received by someone is taken into their hands, so this piece goes inside the next

parts.note: a tiller works the soil
on as written, then P for page

explanation.surface: A High Court order, a single page of it, has been delivered to a gardener.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition and the wordplay both read as one scene; the gardener is a tiller, one who tills the soil.
explanation.definitionFit: An Anton Piller order is a court order allowing search and seizure of evidence without warning, named after a 1976 case.

clue.text: Traditional American individual, about 50, with jaunty lid

indicators.note: one thing about another goes around it, so the outer word holds the rest

parts.note: one single person

indicators.note: a jaunty hat is worn at a rakish angle, so the letters are knocked askew

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
taken as written

explanation.surface: A conventional American fellow of about fifty wears a hat at a jaunty angle.
explanation.walkthrough: ONE goes around L plus the rearranged lid, after its O.
explanation.definitionFit: Old-line is American usage for conservative or long-established, a synonym of traditional.

clue.text: United yarn spun with a single component

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for United, as in football club names

indicators.note: spinning twists things round, so the letters come out in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Several threads joined into one yarn are spun to give a single strand.
explanation.definitionFit: Unary means consisting of one element or taking one operand, i.e. having one part.

clue.text: Flanker making interception in clean tackle

indicators.note: an interception grabs something passing through, so the answer is caught within the following words

parts.note: spanning the end of clean and the start of tackle

explanation.surface: A rugby flanker intercepts the ball with a clean tackle.
explanation.walkthrough: Flanker is a rugby forward in the surface, but the definition is architectural.
explanation.definitionFit: An anta is a pilaster at the end of a side wall, standing at the flank of a doorway or portico.

clue.text: A Moomin novel learner follows, consisting of one word only

indicators.note: something novel is new and different, so the letters take a fresh arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
L is the learner plate; it follows the rest

explanation.surface: A learner reader follows a Moomin novel written in single words.
explanation.walkthrough: Moomins are the troll characters of Tove Jansson's Finnish children's books.
explanation.definitionFit: Monomial is used of a name or expression made of a single term, as opposed to binomial.

clue.text: One practising psychotherapy, I use rolling in hospital bed

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so the mixed letters go within the bed

parts.note: a cot is a hospital bed

indicators.note: rolling things tumble over, so the letters come out mixed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A therapist explains rolling patients about in a hospital bed.
explanation.walkthrough: Émile Coué taught healing by autosuggestion: 'every day in every way I am getting better'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Coueist follows Coué's method of autosuggestion, an early form of psychological therapy.

clue.text: Showy plant, a flag planted in miraculous venue

indicators.note: something planted in the ground goes inside it, so these pieces go within the place

parts.note: Cana is where Jesus turned water into wine
a as written, and a rag is a flag

explanation.surface: A flamboyant plant and a flag are planted at a miraculous site.
explanation.walkthrough: A RAG goes inside CANA after its C.
explanation.definitionFit: Caragana is a flowering shrub of the pea family, the pea tree, grown for its yellow blooms.

clue.text: I lost pity and almost declined old rebuke

indicators.note: losing a letter means it is taken away from the word

parts.note: as in 'it's a sin', a pity

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: ebbed, fell away

explanation.surface: Someone lost sympathy and nearly refused an old reprimand.
explanation.walkthrough: SIN without its I gives SN; EBBED without its last letter gives EBBE.
explanation.definitionFit: Snebbe is an obsolete form of snub, meaning to reprimand or check sharply.

clue.text: One sails northward in company describing islands?

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so these pieces go within the group

parts.note: a set of people, company
a, one

indicators.note: in a down entry, heading north means reading upwards, so the word is written backwards

parts.note: a ship's rig is its sails and masts

explanation.surface: A lone yachtsman sails north in company, perhaps among islands.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the sails turn round, not the whole. The question mark admits that the word describes islands among other things.
explanation.definitionFit: Seagirt means surrounded by the sea, a poetic adjective naturally applied to islands.

clue.text: Ornithologist turned up feather shaft, damn peculiar

parts.note: the rib is the shaft of a feather, here read upwards

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means read from the bottom, so the word runs backwards
peculiar means odd or out of the ordinary, so the letters are put in an unusual order

parts.note: the letters of damn rearranged

explanation.surface: A bird expert finds the shaft of a feather bent upward, which is damned odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Birdman is an informal word for someone who studies or keeps birds, as well as for an aviator.

clue.text: Poet's handle: 'past its best' where English is involved

indicators.note: something involved is wrapped up within, so this letter goes inside the word

parts.note: stale, no longer fresh
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A poet's pen name is said to be past its best where English is concerned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poet's' marks Spenser's word; handle reads as a nickname but is the handle of a tool.
explanation.definitionFit: Steale is Spenser's spelling of steal or stale, the long handle or shaft of a tool.

clue.text: Oral tumour oozing pus, i.e. round front of lip

indicators.note: letters round another go about it, so the other letter is enclosed among them
something oozing flows out of shape, so the letters lose their order

parts.note: taken as written
the letters of the abbreviation

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of lip

explanation.surface: A mouth tumour discharges pus, that is, around the front of the lip.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as a description of the answer, but the definition is just the first two words; the letters are then mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: An epulis is a benign growth on the gum, so a tumour found in the mouth.

clue.text: One gets in after expected time, fuzzy

indicators.note: something that gets in goes inside, so this piece is placed within the other

parts.note: late, arriving after the due time
an, one

explanation.surface: Someone gets in after the expected time, feeling hazy.
explanation.walkthrough: Fuzzy reads as muddled, which suits the latecomer, but here it means downy.
explanation.definitionFit: Lanate is a botanical term for woolly, covered in soft hairs, so fuzzy in texture.

clue.text: Extract of wool half made with torn rags

indicators.note: half a word keeps two of its four letters and drops the rest, here the first pair

parts.note: taken as written; only its back half stays

indicators.note: torn things are ripped apart, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An extract of wool is half made from torn rags.
explanation.definitionFit: Degras is fat recovered from sheepskins, a greasy extract related to wool fat or lanolin.

clue.text: Dragonfly died on motorway, tail missing

indicators.note: with its tail missing a word loses its last letter

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for died
an artery is a major road

explanation.surface: A dragonfly died on the motorway, its tail torn off.
explanation.walkthrough: ARTERY loses its Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Darter is a common name for several dragonflies, from their quick darting flight.

clue.text: Extremes of accent in an Italian maybe, displaying a strong one

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so these letters go within the name

parts.note: Marco is an Italian man's name

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its outer letters, first and last

parts.note: the first and last letters of accent

explanation.surface: An Italian man speaks with a strong accent at both ends of his words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' looks back to accent, so the definition means having a strong accent.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcato is a musical direction meaning marked, each note played with emphasis or stress.

clue.text: Combine in bit of work in muddled group cutting lee

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so this piece goes within the remainder
cutting something takes it away, so these letters are removed from the word

parts.note: a melee is a confused crowd
taken as written, then removed
the erg is a unit of work

explanation.surface: A combine harvester works in a muddled group cutting on the sheltered side.
explanation.walkthrough: The lee to be cut is literally the last three letters of the muddled group, not the sheltered side.
explanation.definitionFit: To merge is to join or blend together, a synonym of combine as a verb.

clue.text: Ingredient of varnish, cloudy, covering stone

parts.note: c is the weather-map abbreviation for cloudy
an opal is a gemstone

explanation.surface: A varnish ingredient makes a cloudy layer covering stone.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, covering means coming on top, so C stands above OPAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Copal is a tropical tree resin used to make varnishes and lacquers.

clue.text: Knockout in G and S? It may be fatal for asses

definitions.text: It may be fatal for asses

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so this word goes between the outer letters

parts.note: the two letters, which also suggest Gilbert and Sullivan
a lander is a heavy blow that lands

explanation.surface: A knockout blow lands in a Gilbert and Sullivan opera, which could be fatal for fools.
explanation.walkthrough: G and S looks like Gilbert and Sullivan, but it is just the two letters. Asses sound like fools; here they are donkeys.
explanation.definitionFit: Glanders is a contagious bacterial disease of horses and donkeys that is often fatal.

clue.text: Soft, old, and heavenly, not real

indicators.note: not means without, so the following word is taken away

parts.note: ethereal, celestial
taken as written, then removed

explanation.surface: Something soft, ancient and heavenly turns out not to be real.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old' marks the archaic word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethe is an obsolete word for easy, so soft in the sense of not hard or difficult.

clue.text: I live without (ultimately) dead parts of intestine

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: to lead a life is to live it

indicators.note: ultimately points to the end, so the last letter is the one meant

parts.note: the final letter of dead

explanation.surface: Someone says they live without dead parts of the gut.
explanation.walkthrough: LEAD loses its D. Ilea is the plural of ileum.
explanation.definitionFit: The ileum is the final section of the small intestine, and ilea is its Latin plural.

clue.text: Grass splits, last coming forward to front

indicators.note: the final letter moves up to the start while the rest keep their order

parts.note: parts, as a verb, splits

explanation.surface: A grass divides, its tip coming forward to the front.
explanation.walkthrough: Grass reads as a verb for inform, but it is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Spart is esparto, a tough grass used for making paper and rope.

clue.text: Mount new production of what's fashionable, including moving set

indicators.note: a word including another holds it inside

parts.note: the rage, the current craze

indicators.note: moving letters shifts them around into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A director mounts a new production of the latest fashionable show, including a moving set.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters go inside RAGE after its R.
explanation.definitionFit: To restage a play is to put it on again in a new production.

clue.text: Measure to beat heroin

parts.note: to cane is to beat with a stick
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: Action is taken to defeat the heroin trade.
explanation.definitionFit: Caneh is a Hebrew unit of length, about six cubits, named from the reed.

clue.text: Information a long time delayed in top military office

parts.note: gen is slang for information
an era is a long period
late, held up

explanation.surface: Intelligence was held up for ages in a high military command.
explanation.definitionFit: A generalate is the rank or office of a general, the highest military command.
